This repo tracks itself with the tool it builds. The session protocol is
`skills/tasks/SKILL.md`, shipped from here. This repo adopts that skill's process and
workspace policy: the task's `process` field, not a generic Superpowers trigger, decides
whether brainstorming runs.

## Gates

Run `just setup` in a fresh checkout or worktree, or after dependency changes. It
uses `work-link` when available to keep target/ off the synced tree, then fetches
the locked Cargo dependencies; safe to rerun.

    just gate

Tests: `just test-one <name>` for a test-name filter, or `just test-one --test cli <name>`
for one integration test; runner arguments are forwarded intact and at least one is
required. This is the local inner loop; run focused tests and mandatory hygiene before
committing. `.tt.toml` disables automatic local `test`, `test-fast`, and `check-code`
execution. Their policy skips have null outcomes and are not passing checks.
`test-fast` selects the fixed non-ignored suite; `test` includes the slow `#[ignore]`d
exhaustive enumeration. `just test-full` is the untimed alias for `TT_FORCE=1 just test`;
`TT_FORCE=1 just check-code` deliberately runs broad Rust checks locally.
Never run `cargo test` directly: the recipe records
the run and stops git discovery at `$TMPDIR`, so a stray `.git` there cannot fail the
fixtures. `just check` composes `just check-hygiene` (`tools/ops-check`,
`tools/ops-docs check`, `tasks check`) and `just check-code` (`cargo fmt --check`,
`cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`). `just ci-check-hygiene` runs the
portable hygiene checks; `tasks check` requires the private detached records repository
and stays on the mandatory local path at every commit and push.
`just docs` regenerates the identity regions of `README.md` and
`AGENTS.md` from `identity.toml`; edit that file, never the regions. Leaf recipes run
through the vendored timing wrapper `tools/tt`; compositions (`check`, `gate`,
`test-full`) add no enclosing timer (ops docs/specs/2026-09-04-test-ci-audit-design.md).
The `hook-pre-commit`, `hook-pre-push`, and `hook-pre-push-fast` timers cover mandatory
hygiene only, then call broad children separately. These durations are incomparable
with the earlier whole-hook timing series. Guide/task-only commits retain hygiene
alone; renames count on both sides and failed classification runs the full check.
On a fresh clone, run `git config core.hooksPath .githooks` once.

The `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs on every branch push (including nested
names) and manual dispatch, on `ubuntu-24.04` with pinned Rust and just. Job-scope
`TT_FORCE=1` runs `just setup`, `just ci-check-hygiene`, `just check-code`, and the full
`just test` suite. Coverage verification derives all executable test targets from
Cargo metadata and requires zero failures, zero ignored tests, and a matching forced
timing record. Covered branch pushes (`refs/heads/*` on `origin`) run mandatory
local hygiene while the hosted workflow carries broad checks and the full suite.
Pushes outside that coverage warn; policy still controls local broad execution.
`tools/tt` reads `.tt.toml` only at the invoking code checkout's Git top level.
`just test-one` and mandatory hygiene always run; `TT_FORCE=1` explicitly forces
broad checks, including nested recipes. A hosted would-be skip without force fails.

Rebuild and reinstall after CLI changes so the tracker used above is the code under test:
`cargo install --locked --path .`

## Layout

- `src/` — `main.rs` / `cli.rs` (clap), `src/commands/` (one module per subcommand, including `resolver.rs` for ids and paths), `model.rs`
  (task record), `frontmatter.rs`, `repo.rs` (tasks/ dir), `registry.rs` (`~/.config/tasks/projects.toml`),
  `locations.rs` (registry location history, path normalization, and the location index behind `resolve`),
  `claims.rs` (out-of-git work claims: the per-prefix store, liveness, and mutation lock),
  `attachments.rs` (tasks/files/<id>/ storage, the attached:/detached: ledger, and the audit behind show and check),
  `clipboard.rs` (wl-paste input for attach),
  `resolve.rs` (spec/plan links), `complete.rs` (shell completion candidates; best-effort, never errors), `query.rs`, `src/output/` / `format.rs` (JSON default, `--pretty`),
  `hierarchy.rs` (parent validation, subtree walks, forest).
- `tests/cli.rs` — end-to-end tests against the built binary in temp repos.
- `tests/attachments.rs` — end-to-end tests for attach, detach, show, check, and rename of task files.
- `justfile`, `tools/tt`, `.githooks/` — the test front door and its timing wrapper (see Gates).
- `identity.toml`, `tools/ops-docs` — the project's declared identity and the vendored
  tool that renders it into both guides and checks their shape (ops
  docs/specs/2026-09-22-project-guides-design.md).
- `tools/cli.toml` — the vendored CLI surface from ops (see `tools/README.md`): the shared
  vocabulary plus a row for every in-scope command and option. `src/surface.rs` builds the
  live parser surface, and its `parser_surface_equals_table` test asserts it matches the
  rows here.
- `skills/tasks/SKILL.md` — the agent skill shipped to other projects; keep it in step with CLI changes.
  `skills/curate/SKILL.md` — the curation pass (`tasks sample`, then bounded edits); same rule.
  `skills/scope/SKILL.md` — the deliberate idea scoping pass; same rule.
- `docs/` — current typed public references; start with [task model](docs/task-model.md)
  and [project operations](docs/project-operations.md). Specs, plans, briefs and handoffs
  live in the project records directory (`tasks where` names it), committed there,
  never in this tree; task links stay relative to records (`--spec` / `--plan --step`).

## Rules

- Any CLI change (a new subcommand, command, or option) starts on ops: land its rows in
  ops's `cli.toml` first, then run
  `python3 "$(tasks --pretty root ops-88a0fa)/bin/vendored" adopt cli.toml` in this
  checkout and commit the vendored copy together with the parser change. Never edit
  `tools/cli.toml` in place (ops-check refuses it) and never hand-copy a table into it:
  `parser_surface_equals_table` fails until the adopted table matches the parser.
- JSON output is the contract; `--pretty` is for humans. Never change JSON shapes without a task.
- Fail early with a typed error; no silent fallbacks.
